숫자를 올리고 종이로 내보냅니다: Put the numbers on and send it to paper
치수 스타일숫자보다 먼저 정한다문자 높이·화살표 크기·소수 자릿수를 한곳: Dimension styleSettle it before the numbersText height, arrow size and decimal places all in one place. Skip it and you end up fixing dimensions one at a time later.
치수 기입손보다 판단이 앞선다전체 크기부터 각도까지 값을 올린다. 무엇을: DimensioningJudgement comes before the handYou put values on, from the overall size down to the angle. What you are measuring decides which command you use.
참고 치수와 수량숫자만으로는 뜻이 안 간다같은 구멍 넷은 앞에 개수를,: Reference dimensions and countsA bare number does not carry the meaningFour identical holes get the count in front; a value nobody will inspect gets brackets. What does not fit comes out on a leader.
축척 확인과 출도화면이 아니라 종이가 기준화면은 마음대로 확대되지만 종이: Checking the scale and releasingPaper is the reference, not the screenThe screen zooms as you please; paper has a fixed size. Look at the scale with your own eyes before it goes out.
무엇을 재느냐가 명령을 정합니다: What you measure decides the command
재는 대상이 명령을 고른다: The thing you measure picks the command
실습에 바로 듣는 값 셋: Three values that bite straight away
문자 높이는 종이에서 읽히느냐를 정하고, 화살표 크기는 문자 높이에 맞춰: Text height decides whether it can be read on paper, and arrow size has to match the text height or one dimension stands apart from the rest. Decimal places change the value you appear to be stating: leave it at 0 and 95.7 becomes 96.
선형은 가로세로 거리, 정렬은 경사면 자체의 길이, 지름은 완전한 원,: Linear is a horizontal or vertical distance, aligned is the true length of a sloped face, diameter is for a full circle, radius for an arc, angular for the angle between two lines. Put a diameter on an arc and the drawing points at a point that is not there.
치수선에 안 들어가는 것: What will not fit on a dimension line
형상이 작아 치수선을 그 안에 넣으면 아무것도 안 보이는 경우, 그리고: When a feature is so small that a dimension line inside it hides everything, and when one line has to carry a count, a thread and a depth together, you point at the feature and write it outside.
재지 말라는 지시: An instruction not to measure it
다른 치수에서 계산돼 따라 나오는 값이라 만들 때만 참고하고 검사할 때는: It follows from other dimensions, so it is for reference while making and is not measured at inspection. You still write it so the reader does not have to work it out by hand every time.
Remember Settle the style first, then pick the command to fit what you are measuring.
같은 120이라도 어디서 쟀느냐가 다릅니다: The same 120 means different things depending on where you measured it
기준면을 정하고 잰다: Fix the datum face, then measure
120은 윗변이 아닌 바닥 변에서. 90의 끝점은 보스 원의 위쪽 사분점: The 120 comes off the bottom edge, not the top. The end of the 90 is the upper quadrant of the boss circle.
Measured from one place on the left edge and one on the bottom. Gather the datums or the errors stack.
There is no corner to catch, so you measure to the end circle centres. The 10 width is already fixed by the R5.
A full circle takes a diameter, an arc a radius. All four run their dimension lines outside the shape.
Not a machined feature but an imaginary circle the tapped-hole centres sit on. The first hole is at 45 degrees.
The brackets mean do not measure it. The 26 is a straight instruction. Thickness is measured in the top view.

치수 기입에서 가장 자주 나오는 넷입니다: The four that come up most when you dimension
치수가 외형선 레이어에 들어가면 흰색으로 나와 형상과 구분이 안 되고,: Dimensions that land on the visible line layer come out white, indistinguishable from the shape, and you can no longer check by toggling that layer. Click one dimension, take the rest with select similar, and move them together.
종이에서 읽히는지 본다: Look at whether it reads on paper
화면에서 멀쩡해도 A3로 뽑으면 깨알만 하거나 형상을 덮는다. 확인은 플: It can look fine on screen and come out as specks, or covering the shape, on A3. The check is the plot preview. If nothing you change makes a difference, the overall scale on the Fit tab is not 1, and that value multiplies everything.
장공에 폭 10과 R5를 같이, 좌우 필렛에 R10을 각각, 정면도와 평: Putting both the 10 width and the R5 on a slot, an R10 on each of the two fillets, the same 120 in both the front and the top view. Fix one and the two say different things, and the maker has to choose.
괄호가 검사 여부를 가른다: The brackets decide whether it is inspected
95.7에 괄호를 빼먹으면 검사 대상이 되는데, 계산돼 나오는 값이라 반: Leave the brackets off 95.7 and it becomes an inspected value — and because it is a computed one, rounding puts it out and a perfectly good part fails. Put brackets on a value that should be inspected and nobody measures it.
How to fix it All four can be checked on this very drawing, right now.
스타일부터 PDF까지: From the style to the PDF
치수 스타일을 새로 만들어 문자 5, 화살표 5, 자릿수 0으로 통일: Created a new dimension style with text 5, arrows 5 and 0 decimal places throughout
가로세로는 선형, 경사면은 정렬, 완전한 원은 지름, 호는 반지름, 벌어: Linear for horizontal and vertical, aligned for a sloped face, diameter for a full circle, radius for an arc, angular for the angle between
120과 90, 16, 60과 62, 29·50·12·8, 목 밑동 80: 120 and 90, 16, 60 and 62, 29·50·12·8 and the 80 web foot, all measured from the datum faces
Ø25 H7, Ø56, 2-R10, 2-R5, PCD Ø44와 45도,: Ø25 H7, Ø56, 2-R10, 2-R5, PCD Ø44 and 45 degrees, thickness 12 and 20, (95.7) and 26
숫자로 안 되는 표기는 지시선으로 2-C5와 4-M5 깊이 10, A3: What a number alone cannot say went out on leaders — 2-C5 and 4-M5 DEPTH 10 — then A3 at 1:1, checked, and out as PDF
레이어를 하나씩 껐다 켜면 무엇이 어느 레이어에 있는지 스스로 검사된다: Toggle the layers one at a time and the drawing checks itself for what sits on which layer
최종 판정은 화면이 아니라 플롯 미리보기다: The final judgement is the plot preview, not the screen
오늘 쓴 값은 지시가 없을 때의 기본값이고, 과제 지시가 언제나 우선한다: The values used today are the defaults when nothing is specified; the task sheet always wins
다른 부품도 순서는 같다. 용도를 읽고, 기준면을 정하고, 그 기준에서: The order is the same for any other part — read what it is for, fix the datum faces, measure from them
도면은 그림이 아니라 지시 문서다. 숫자 하나가 이만큼 깎으라는 문장이었: A drawing is an instruction, not a picture. Each number was a sentence saying cut this much
명령보다 상황을 기억하세요: Remember the situation, not the command
매 차시 지난 상태에서 이어 그릴 때: To carry on from the previous state
스냅이 어디 붙었는지 봐야 할 때: To see where a snap landed
객체 스냅 항목을 정한다: Chooses which object snaps are on
끝점·중심·접점을 정확히 잡아야 할 때: To catch an endpoint, centre or tangent exactly
낱개로 다뤄야 하는 조각. 뒤에 자르거나 둥글릴 선: Pieces you need singly — to trim or round later
선 종류·색상을 개체가 아니라 레이어로 정할 때: When linetype and color belong to the layer
문자 높이·화살표·소수 자릿수를 도면 축척에 맞출 때: To match text, arrows and decimals to the drawing scale
수평·수직 치수를 넣는다: Puts on a horizontal or vertical dimension
가로 세로로 잰 값: A value measured across or up
무한히 뻗는 구성선을 긋는다: Draws a construction line that runs on forever
투상선. 도면에 남기지 않고 뷰를 맞출 때: Projectors. To line views up and not leave them
구성선만 골라 지울 때: To pick out only the construction lines
기울어진 변에 나란한 치수를 넣는다: A dimension parallel to a sloped edge
경사면의 실제 길이: The true length of a sloped face
지시선과 문자를 넣는다: Puts on a leader with text
도형 밖에서 끌어와 설명할 때: To say it outside the shape
종이나 PDF 로 내보낼 때: When it goes out to paper or PDF
